summary: Describes textual conventions and OBJECT-IDENTITIES used in managing ATM-based interfaces, devices, networks and services. Other ATM MIB modules reuse these shared definitions.

eli5.summary: Different ATM management documents need to use the same words for the same things. This document is the shared vocabulary they all borrow from.

questions: what atm traffic descriptor types exist
subtitle: A shared vocabulary of types and traffic descriptors for managing ATM networks with SNMP MIBs.

tldr.problem: Several ATM management MIB modules need the same kinds of values, such as ATM addresses, connection kinds and traffic descriptors, and each should not define them separately.
tldr.mechanism: This memo defines the ATM-TC-MIB module, a set of textual conventions with precise meanings and a set of OBJECT-IDENTITY values that name ATM traffic descriptor types.
tldr.outcome: Other ATM MIB modules import these definitions. The memo itself says security issues are addressed in the memos that define those modules.

today: RFC 2514 is a Proposed Standard from February 1999, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the home of the shared ATM textual conventions and traffic descriptor identities.

sections.title: Purpose of the Module
sections.content:
RFC 2514 defines textual conventions and OBJECT-IDENTITIES used for managing ATM-based interfaces, devices, networks and services. A textual convention is a new type that has a different name and a similar syntax to an SMI type, but a more precise meaning, for the convenience of humans reading a MIB module. They are defined as in RFC 1903.

The OBJECT-IDENTITY macro, from RFC 1902, registers further properties under object identifier assignments so other MIB modules can use them.

For organizational purposes, the OBJECT-IDENTITIES previously defined in RFC 1695 were moved here and no longer appear in the revision of that RFC. The original OBJECT IDENTIFIERs were preserved.
sections.eli5: Instead of every ATM document inventing its own words, this one holds the common words in one place. Some words were moved here from an older document without changing their numbers.

sections.title: The ATM-TC-MIB Module
sections.content:
The definitions are one MIB module, ATM-TC-MIB, identified as atmTCMIB and placed at { mib-2 37 3 }. It was last updated in 9810190200Z by the IETF AToMMIB Working Group. It imports MODULE-IDENTITY, OBJECT-IDENTITY, TimeTicks and mib-2 from SNMPv2-SMI, and TEXTUAL-CONVENTION from SNMPv2-TC.

The textual conventions are listed alphabetically. The OBJECT-IDENTITIES follow them, with new ones defined under atmObjectIdentities at { atmTCMIB 1 }.
sections.eli5: All the definitions live in one module with its own number, like one chapter in a big manual.

sections.title: Addresses and Interface Types
sections.content:
AtmAddr is an ATM address as an octet string of 0 to 40 octets, where the length implies the type: no address (0 octets), E.164 (8 octets) or NSAP (20 octets). A subaddress can be appended, giving E.164 plus E.164 (16 octets), E.164 plus NSAP (28 octets) or NSAP plus NSAP (40 octets). The E.164 address is encoded in BCD format.

AtmIlmiNetworkPrefix is the prefix used for ILMI address registration, 8 or 13 octets long. For ATM end system addresses it is the first 13 octets, covering the AFI, IDI and HO-DSP fields. For a native E.164 address it is the whole address in 8 octets.

AtmInterfaceType says which connection setup procedures an interface uses. Its 13 values run from other(1) and autoConfig(2) through ITU-T DSS2, ATM Forum UNI 3.0, 3.1 and 4.0, IISP variants, PNNI 1.0 and B-ICI 2.0, to atmfUniPvcOnly(12) and atmfNniPvcOnly(13), which are compliant interfaces with signalling disabled.
sections.eli5: Some of these words describe the street address of a device and which set of manners it uses when starting a call.

sections.title: Connections, Identifiers and Status
sections.content:
AtmConnCastType gives a connection's topology: p2p(1), p2mpRoot(2) or p2mpLeaf(3). AtmConnKind gives the call control used: pvc(1), svcIncoming(2), svcOutgoing(3), spvcInitiator(4) or spvcTarget(5). A PVC link is always cross-connected to a PVC link, and an incoming SVC link to an outgoing one.

AtmServiceCategory lists other, cbr, rtVbr, nrtVbr, abr and ubr. AtmVpIdentifier ranges 0 to 4095 and AtmVcIdentifier 0 to 65535. For ATM UNIs the VPI ranges from 0 to 255 and for NNIs from 0 to 4095.

Index types AtmSigDescrParamIndex and AtmTrafficDescrParamIndex run 0 to 2147483647, where 0 means no row applies or none was identified. AtmVorXAdminStatus is up or down, AtmVorXOperStatus adds unknown, and AtmVorXLastChange is a TimeTicks value of sysUpTime when the link last changed state, or zero if that was before the last agent re-initialization.
sections.eli5: These words say how a connection is shaped, what kind of call set it up, which numbered lane it uses and whether it is turned on.

sections.title: Traffic Descriptor Identities
sections.content:
The OBJECT-IDENTITIES name the possible ATM traffic descriptor types. The subtree atmTrafficDescriptorTypes sits at { mib-2 37 1 1 }, moved from RFC 1695, and holds identities numbered 1 to 15 such as atmNoClpNoScr, atmNoClpScr and atmClpTaggingScrCdvt.

Each describes how up to five parameters are used. These can include peak cell rate in cells/second, sustainable cell rate, maximum burst size in cells, minimum cell rate and CDVT in tenths of microseconds. Unused parameters are marked as not used. Several refer to conformance definitions such as CBR.1, VBR.1, VBR.2, VBR.3, UBR.1 and UBR.2.

Three are marked deprecated: atmNoTrafficDescriptor, atmClpNoTaggingNoScr and atmClpTaggingNoScr. The CLP-transparent ones are rejected at UNI 3.0 or UNI 3.1 interfaces, with an alternative pointed out in each description.
sections.eli5: Each of these is a named recipe for describing how much data a connection may send and how fast, with a few settings per recipe.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo defines only textual conventions and object identities for use in ATM MIB modules. It says that security issues for those MIB modules are addressed in the memos defining them, so it contains nothing further itself.
sections.eli5: This dictionary has no secrets to guard. The documents that actually use the words handle safety.

items.label: svcIncoming
items.desc: Link established after a received signaling request to set up an SVC.

items.label: svcOutgoing
items.desc: Link established after a transmitted or forwarded signaling request to set up an SVC.

items.label: spvcInitiator
items.desc: PVC side of an SVC/PVC crossconnect where the switch initiates the Soft PVC setup.

items.label: spvcTarget
items.desc: PVC side of an SVC/PVC crossconnect where the switch is the target of the Soft PVC setup.
